task_instance: Given a Claude Code development-session transcript (JSONL) for a project, extract the narrative arc and write a structured BLOG-NOTES.md at the project root, following the skill's template (Title Ideas, Hook, Act Structure, Key Quotes, Technical Highlights, Lessons Learned).
evidence: Created a small realistic input transcript (the INPUT a user supplies): sample-project/.claude/projects/-Users-dev-rate-limiter/session-abc123.jsonl, a 10-line JSONL Claude Code session about building a token-bucket rate limiter, including the reported concurrency bug, the user's explicit course-correction (one lock per key, not a global lock), the memory-eviction follow-up, and the sign-off. Read that transcript in full and synthesized the deliverable at sample-project/BLOG-NOTES.md. The skill is a pure text-to-text transformation; its bash snippets (ls/wc/rg/jq) and Task subagents are only suggested helpers for locating/chunking large transcripts, and no bundled script, template, or reference file is required or missing. Verified the deliverable by confirming it contains every section the skill's template prescribes (Title Ideas, The Hook, Act Structure as 5 beats, Key Quotes, Technical Highlights, Lessons Learned) and that each element traces to the transcript: the race-condition bug, the verbatim 'use one lock per key' quote, the exactly-100-pass/50-reject test result, and the eviction sweep. No shell/code execution, network, or MCP tools were used; all work was reading and writing text files inside the work directory.
